event: Weekly Market Review
title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Defensive rotation week; utilities and staples bid, semiconductors unwound hard.

Money moved out of AI hardware and into yield-sensitives, defensives and real assets: SOXX -5.01% against XLU +3.97% and XLP +3.60%, with gold +1.17%. Friday's Michigan consumer confidence miss (46.3 vs 47.8 forecast) and one-year inflation expectations at 4.7% bracketed the week — weak demand, sticky prices — while Thursday's 10-year auction cleared at 5.3% vs 4.83% prior, keeping the pressure on long duration.

INDICES — SPY +1.16%, DIA +0.98%, QQQ +0.23%, IWM -0.92%. Large beat small by 1.86pp (RSP +1.58% vs IJR -0.70%): cap-weight lagged equal-weight, so the week was broad, not mega-cap. VIX closed 14.8, below its 15.7 20-day average — vol fell. Biggest cross-asset move: WTI +1.85% Friday (USO), with nat-gas UNG +1.85% and the dollar UUP +0.14% grinding higher. 35% of S&P 500 names sit above their 50-day, 47% above the 200-day — the average stock is not extended.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLU Utilities +3.97%, XLP Staples +3.60%, XLE Energy +3.60%, XLV Health Care +2.79%, XLY Discretionary +2.55%, XLF Financials +2.32%, XLRE Real Estate +1.96%, XLB Materials +1.17%, XLC Comm Services +0.05%, XLI Industrials -0.41%, XLK Technology -0.52%. Top industries: UTES +7.39%, UNG +5.16%; bottom: DRAM -7.43%, WGMI -11.25%. Money went in XLU (+$2,313mm, 100th pctile) and XLK (+$1,771mm); out of SOXX (-$2,328mm, 0th pctile) and DIA. Rotation state: defensive risk-off.

DRIVERS — Semis were the week's funding source: SOXX -5.01%, SMH -4.32%, DRAM -7.43%, WGMI -11.25%, and SOXX saw the heaviest thematic outflow at the 0th percentile. That capital landed in utilities, staples and energy while the long end stayed hostile (10-year auction tailed to 5.3%). Crypto-adjacent and memory names led the downside; KWEB +4.48% on 2.2x volume was the one high-beta pocket that caught a bid. Gold +1.17% and the dollar's 20-day +3.38% gain both say the same thing: investors want collateral, not duration.

WHAT'S NEXT — Vol is compressed (VIX 14.8 under its 20-day; S&P ATM IV 6.8%) while election-adjacent CPI lands Oct 14 with headline forecast at 3.60% year-over-year versus 3.40% prior — a hot print re-prices the long end and pressures the utilities/staples bid that just went to the 100th percentile. Semis sit on a 20-day gain of 6.13% despite the -5.01% week, the classic setup for a reflex bounce or a continued unwind. IWM's 0.37 put/call ratio and max-pain at 280 flag a small-cap positioning squeeze potential heading into Oct 28.

Word count: ~430.
